I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because in Quzhou this is the most steady way for me to protect grain output, use my irrigation water carefully, and avoid taking on too much market risk. At the start of the season, my winter wheat is already the main crop I am managing, so I will push it through to harvest with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and only necessary pesticide sprays. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly on the same land, because it matches our local heat and rainfall better than most other options and lets me use the full year well. I will use improved or hybrid seed instead of old saved seed, because I care more about stable yield and lodging resistance than saving a little on seed. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat preparation and mostly no-tillage or very light tillage before maize after wheat, because that saves time and helps me catch the planting window. I will not spread inputs blindly. I will keep nitrogen moderate, add phosphorus and potassium to hold the soil, irrigate wheat more than maize, and spray only when pests or disease pressure justify it. My goal is steady harvest and lower risk, not chasing the very highest yield.
